title: Arkret Common ID and Reference Definitions
description: Shared ID and reference pattern $defs referenced cross-file by multiple object schemas so a single form change propagates without inline drift. Defs-only: not an object or event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md and artifacts/registry/id-kind-registry.json for the authoritative ID kind registry.

event_id.description: Complete Arkret Event cryptographic identity. The suffix is the canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of exactly 33 octets: one registered active digest-suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of the Event digest. Regex validation is only lexical; receivers MUST decode, require 33 octets, canonical re-encode, and verify the suite code and full digest before use.

realm_commit_id.description: Content-addressed identity of a closed unsigned RealmCommit body. The suffix uses the fixed v1 digest suite and the same canonical 33-octet token encoding as Event IDs.

realm_authority_handoff_id.description: Content-addressed identity of one closed old-to-new Realm authority handoff.

realm_snapshot_id.description: Content-addressed identity of an authority-signed typed Realm snapshot.

mls_group_id.description: RFC 9420 group_id as base64url_no_pad(SHA-256(UTF8("ak.mls.group_id.v1") || 0x00 || canonical_effective_scope_key_bytes(effective_scope))), so exactly 43 characters. Derived by the reducer and the SDK from the effective scope alone; actors never submit it. The v1 formula is the only one: the earlier reversible base64url of the scope key bytes MUST NOT be accepted alongside it. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.2.

push_target_id.description: Canonical typed pairwise push pseudonym. The suffix is the unpadded Base64URL encoding of the complete 32-octet HMAC-SHA256 output for one (recipient_id, principal_id, device_id, push_route, salt_epoch_id) tuple. Receivers MUST decode exactly 32 octets and require canonical re-encoding; it is never a DID, object id, raw provider token, or stable cross-service correlation key.

account_status_record_id.description: Account Authority issuer-ledger record identity derived from the complete closed unsigned AccountStatusRecord core.

account_id.description: Complete protocol identity for a principal at one Station, including human, Agent, Applet-managed Ghost and integration accounts. It does not imply a human login, provisioning workflow, credential class or authorization. Equality is byte-for-byte equality of both canonical did_core_id components; neither component may be inferred from a DID Document, route, session audience, current service, handle, or local database key. Accounts with the same principal_id at different station_id values are permanently distinct. Principal equality MUST NOT establish account equivalence or any permission inheritance, merging, delegation, substitution or recovery relationship. Account-scoped authority requires independent authorization for the exact AccountId. Permanent loss of a Station does not permit its accounts or PCR lineages to migrate to or revive at another Station; Realm takeover and RealmCommit recovery do not waive this boundary. See models/common-fields.md section 4.2.

actor_id.description: Complete protocol identity for an Event author or Realm member: account carries the exact AccountId for every Station-hosted principal; service identifies a service acting as itself. The discriminator is validated against accepted registration and admission evidence; it never authorizes itself. Account and service are distinct, and no comparison may fall back to a bare principal_id. Agent and integration classification, provisioning, controller binding and credential authorization are independently verified facts, not identity variants. Account actors at different Stations MUST NOT share or inherit authority merely because their principal_id, DID controller or signing key matches, including membership, capability, RealmCommit-signing and recovery authority.

web_origin.description: Canonical HTTP(S) Web Origin: lowercase scheme/host plus an optional valid non-default effective port. Userinfo, path (including a trailing slash), query, fragment, explicit :80 on HTTP, and explicit :443 on HTTPS are forbidden.

blob_id.description: Producer-allocated identity of one Blob metadata resource. A blob_id never commits to content bytes and MUST NOT be used where a content-addressed blob_ref is required.

blob_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to exact Blob bytes. The embedded suite and digest are the sole wire commitment to those bytes; sibling content/ciphertext digest mirrors are forbidden.

did_core_id.description: Canonical stable DID-derived identity core. The lowercase DID method name follows ak:did_core:, and the remaining method-adapter-defined core is opaque to generic consumers. The did:web v1 adapter uses the complete canonical method-specific-id, never a digest or truncated host. Principal-core and service-core equality is byte-for-byte equality of the complete did_core_id. Event actor and Realm membership equality instead use the complete closed ActorId, and account-scoped equality uses the complete AccountId; neither may be reduced to a principal core. A did_core_id is not a DID and cannot be resolved without a did or AuthenticatedServiceResolution.

did.description: Canonical bare DID used for registration, DID method resolution and owner-published current resolution. It contains no path, query or fragment and MUST project through the registered method adapter to exactly one did_core_id.

webvh_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identifier used at method-native registration, document and evidence boundaries. Role admission is enforced separately.

human_principal_did.description: Canonical bare DID for a v1 human principal anchor. The method set is derived from role_requirements.human_principal_anchor and contains exactly did:webvh. Every other method, including did:key and did:web, MUST fail closed with unsupported_did_method here rather than inside a method parser or history replay. Capability checks for relocation, DID-root recovery and ongoing governance are separate.

agent_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identity of a durable Agent. Its accepted bootstrap history is controller-authored and must contain a continuous inception followed by the create-locked PCR binding update.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet installation identity. Applet service authority is carried separately by service_id.

applet_managed_actor_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identity of an Applet-managed Bot or Ghost. Its inception is committed by the immutable Applet-managed actor provision Event and the cross-bound applet_managed_control PCR genesis.

did_key_did.description: Canonical bare did:key identifier used at method-native key and witness evidence boundaries. This is a registered method-specific Did subtype, not a business ActorId and not a DID URL.

did_url.description: Arkret verification-method DID URL profile (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2): lowercase method name, no query, required fragment, fragment limited to ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. Every verification_method-family field and every kid/key_ref a schema declares to be a DID URL MUST resolve to exactly this definition; values compare byte-for-byte with no URI normalization or percent-decoding.
